text:
anya: Quick heads up — we're planning to enable hazel-7b-quantv2 in the model catalog tomorrow during the 02:00 UTC changewindow. Need alignment on fallback ordering and pin strategy before I flip the switch.
deploy-bot: changewindow reserved: 2025-11-12 02:00 UTC (window id cw-20251112-02). Please ack. :calendar:
kevin: ack. i prefer fallback ordering: 1) orchid-13b-compat (same architecture, likely best fidelity), 2) harbor-13b-legacy (higher token quality historically), 3) tiny-7b-fallback (lower-cost, last resort). keep the quant variants lower priority.
sam g: agree with kevin. also recommend pinning enterprise customers to orchid-13b-compat for 48h to avoid surprise cost/quality shifts. we should add a note in the rollout spreadsheet.
julie: telemetry gates: start at 1% traffic for 30m, then 10% for 1h, then 50% for 2h if metrics look good. primary signals: p50 latency, p95 latency, error rate, quality-regression on the smoke promptset. gating rule: if quality-reg drops >1.5% or error rate >1% -> automatic pause.
mike: canary plan sounds good. define quality-regression: compare model scoring on the curated eval set (script: `scripts/eval/compare_shot.py --baseline orchid-13b-compat --candidate hazel-7b-quantv2`). If delta > 1.5% on Rouge/LR metrics -> rollback.
ops_oncall: i'll be oncall for the window. add me to the rollout doc and the PagerDuty runbook. my rollback steps: 1) pin catalog fallback to orchid-13b-compat, 2) drain hazel variant, 3) revert deployment via deploybot. example commands below:
```
# pin fallback
redwoodctl catalog set-fallback --model hazel-7b-quantv2 --order orchid-13b-compat,harbor-13b-legacy,tiny-7b-fallback
# rollback
deploybot rollback --catalog hazel-7b-quantv2 --reason "quality regression"
```
ops_oncall: i'll keep the zoom link open and watch the telemetry. please post links to dashboards before we start.
anya: i'll add the dashboards: latency dashboard, error-rate, and the eval diff dashboard. Julie — can you paste direct links and the smoke promptset name?
julie: links: https://console.redwood/telemetry/dashboards/latency-hazel https://console.redwood/telemetry/dashboards/err-hazel https://console.redwood/telemetry/dashboards/eval-diff-hazel smoke set: `rollout_smoke_v2`
mike: release note copy for product & enterprise teams: "Enabling hazel-7b-quantv2 (quantized performance-oriented variant). Fallback ordering: orchid-13b-compat -> harbor-13b-legacy -> tiny-7b-fallback. Canary 1% -> 10% -> 50%. Telemetry gates applied; expect small cost improvements. Contact ops@redwood if you see regressions."
sam g: pls make sure enterprise customers pinned to orchid-13b-compat get an email 24h beforehand. i can draft.
anya: added email task. deploy-bot, please schedule the enable with the fallback ordering and canary config.
deploy-bot: schedule accepted: job id jb-5935012345-01. canary rollout: 1% x30m, 10% x60m, 50% x120m. fallback order set as requested. will post status updates to this thread.
kevin: one more: add a tolerance on cost-per-token spike >30% during canary to pause automatically.
julie: done — added cost spike rule and a soft alert at 20%.
anya: thanks all — i'll be the release lead. ops_oncall will own rollback. tagging @deploy-bot to kick at 02:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: started canary (1%) at 2025-11-12T02:00:00Z — job jb-5935012345-01. monitoring enabled.
anya: thanks — will watch the thread and call rollback if we hit gates.
